youtube.title: What the US Government Actually Says About the Bermuda Triangle
youtube.description:
The Bermuda Triangle, a stretch of the western Atlantic between Florida, Bermuda and the Caribbean, is linked to famous losses like the USS Cyclops (1918) and Flight 19 (1945), when five Navy bombers with 14 men vanished, followed by a rescue plane with 13 more. A Navy report said it was "as if they had flown to Mars." But the name itself was coined only in 1964, by writer Vincent Gaddis in a magazine article, and a 1974 bestseller by Charles Berlitz turned it into a legend. The US Coast Guard says "no extraordinary factors have ever been identified," and NOAA says there is no evidence that disappearances happen more often there than in other heavily traveled ocean areas.
